messages:
alex: Heads-up — main is CI-red intermittently on TestStreamInterleave. First popped up after 7f4a2cd (merge from feature/stream-mux). Failing on macos-latest and ubuntu-22.04 runners. Example failure chunk:

```
E       AssertionError: packet order mismatch
E       Expected: [pktA, pktB, pktC]
E       Actual:   [pktB, pktA, pktC]

/opt/hostedtoolcache/.cargo/bin/pytest tests/test_stream_interleave.py::TestStreamInterleave::test_packet_order -q
```

Any quick eyes? Might be nondet interleaving between StreamMuxer and the async sender.

priya: I saw one flop on my branch earlier. Kicked a CI rerun: https://ci.redwood/runs/78234 (rerun queued). Can someone try a local repro?

ci-bot: Re-run job #78234 queued by priya — ETA ~5m :white_check_mark:

jamie: Hypothesis: race when we flush KV cache and resume session => two partial streams get merged out of order. I can try running with REDWOOD_STREAM_DEBUG=1 and `RUST_TEST_THREADS=1` to force single-thread ordering to see if it stabilizes. Local quick command: 

```
REDWOOD_STREAM_DEBUG=1 RUST_TEST_THREADS=1 cargo test -p runtime --test stream_interleave -- --nocapture -k packet_order
```

alex: @jamie awesome — can you paste the minimal repro command if you get one? If it's flaky locally, we can bisect commits.

priya: If someone can bisect, that'd speed things up. I can run a git-bisect job across last 60 commits today. Steps I plan: `git bisect start -- bad 7f4a2cd -- good HEAD~60` then run `./dev/repro/stream_interleave.sh` that runs the test 20x per commit. Any objections?

jamie: No objections. One tip: add a small artificial yield in StreamMuxer (sleep 1ms) to amplify the window — helps repro. I used that to get a 100% repro locally once.

sloane: Can we mark the test flaky in CI temporarily so it doesn't block merges while we debug? Maybe use `CI_FLAKY_ALLOW=1` for that job or add `xfail` in pytest with a TODO. We should also pin rollout so customer traffic isn't affected (if this impacts serving).

alex: Fine with temporary flaky marker, but let's avoid reverting the whole merge yet. Priya — go ahead with bisect and post results here. Jamie — if you get a deterministic repro, push a small patch to a debug branch so we can run the CI matrix.

priya: Starting bisect now, I'll post periodic updates. First run: testing commit 7f4a2cd (bad) vs good at HEAD~60. Running the harness: `./dev/repro/stream_interleave.sh --runs 20` — will share logs.

jamie: Quick note — when you share logs, include the header with runner (macos vs ubuntu) and the env vars; the failure differs by platform sometimes.

alex: Thanks all. If bisect narrows to a suspect, assign a small revert or targeted fix. Ping me if you need bandwidth for CI env changes.

priya: Update (10m): bisect found the first failing commit: 7f4a2cd -> introducing StreamMuxer changes. Narrowing to the exact patch within that merge now. Will share a short summary after one more pass.

jamie: Nice — if it's in that merge, I can take a look at the orderer code tomorrow and try the 1ms yield trick to confirm.

sloane: I'll open a quick CI patch to mark the test flaky on macos only so merges aren't blocked while we have a targeted fix.

alex: Great progress — please keep logs here. :thumbsup:
